access_control.title: Access control
access_control.subtitle: Decide which destinations users can access through native nodes.

help.label: About {{name}}
help.policies:
Access control is enforced by nodes; blocked connections are disconnected. The rule library only determines client routing, which users can change themselves. Only PSP native nodes enforce these policies; operators manage 3X-UI and S-UI routing themselves.

Rules are evaluated from top to bottom and stop at the first match. After an observation match, later rules do not apply to that connection. Ordering within one action only determines the policy name attributed to the match; place blocking policies that count toward risk above others.

Nodes can see the destination (domain or IP), but cannot see URL paths. Policies can be bypassed with ECH, resolving through DoH then connecting directly to an IP, or a client's own encrypted tunnel.

IP ranges apply only to connections initiated with an IP; IPs resolved from domain names do not participate in matching. BT detection only recognizes plaintext handshakes and uTP; encrypted BT and DHT cannot be detected.

Regular expressions are matched individually for every connection and consume resources; the limit is {{max_regexps}}.

Each deployment restarts the node's proxy once and interrupts active connections once. Deployment waits {{seconds}} seconds after the last change; consecutive changes are combined into one deployment.
help.lists:
Supported formats: plain domains; domain: / full: / keyword: / regexp:; *.x; hosts lines; AdGuard ||x^; Clash rules; IPs and IP ranges. Lines beginning with # are comments. Saving lowercases domains, removes trailing dots, converts international domain names to punycode and aligns IP ranges to their network address.

Remote and category lists refresh every {{hours}} hours. Only changed content is deployed; failed refreshes keep the previous content.

Broad entries (expressions matching almost all domains, keywords shorter than four characters, public suffixes themselves and excessively large IP ranges) are excluded from custom lists and community categories, with a parse report. A remote URL list containing them fails the entire refresh and keeps its previous content. Community categories also keep previous content when filtering leaves no entries; a first download remains unready. Excluded entries are never deployed.

geo_anomaly.scope_hint: How fine the judgement goes: "City, tiered" judges countries, regions and cities; "Region / state" skips cities; "Country only" judges countries alone.
geo_anomaly.max_places: Country tolerance: countries allowed at once
geo_anomaly.max_places_hint: 1 means two countries at once is over.
geo_anomaly.max_regions: Region tolerance: regions allowed at once in one country
geo_anomaly.max_regions_hint: 1 means two regions of one country at once is over. A home router plus a phone in another region also trips it; raise to 2 if noisy.
geo_anomaly.max_cities: City tolerance: cities allowed at once in one country
geo_anomaly.max_cities_hint: 2 means three cities of one country at once is over; addresses placed only to a country never count as a city.
geo_anomaly.effective: In effect: over at {{countries}} countries, or {{regions}} regions, or {{cities}} cities in one country
geo_anomaly.min_placed_ratio_hint: Below this share of locatable addresses the verdict is "unknown", so a stale or partial database cannot quietly read as a clean fleet.
geo_anomaly.flag_after_hint: One noisy sample does not raise an alert — below this it shows as "suspect". Setting it to 1 disables hysteresis and makes the detector flap; not recommended.
geo_anomaly.clear_after_hint: Keep it above the checks to flag, or an account sheds its flag by stepping under the line for one check. Being disconnected does not count toward clearing.
geo_anomaly.co_travel_hint: One set per line, country codes comma-separated (any case). Countries only; region or city entries containing "/" are ignored. A third country outside the set still flags.
geo_anomaly.allow_anywhere: Allow anywhere in this scope (no detection)
geo_anomaly.allow_anywhere_hint: An outright exemption rather than a raised threshold — raising the threshold would also loosen detection for everyone who is not travelling. Set it on one group to exempt only that group.
geo_anomaly.ignore_addresses_hint: One per line or comma-separated, up to 256; text after # is a comment. For relays, CDNs or office exits the panel does not know. Node and relay addresses, 100.64.0.0/10 and private ranges, and addresses held at once by at least the shared-exit account count (3 by default) are excluded automatically. Global only.
geo_anomaly.ban_hint: When on, accounts that stay over the suspension thresholds have proxy service suspended and restored automatically when the time is up. Panel login is kept, no other suspension is overwritten, and accounts in an emergency window, expired or over quota are never auto-suspended. An account still over the line after it is restored is suspended again — trust a confirmed false positive from its risk details. Thresholds are raised to at least the flag tolerances.
geo_anomaly.ban_tolerance_hint: Same meaning as the country, region and city tolerances, used only for suspension.
geo_anomaly.ban_after_hint: Manual polls closer than half a poll interval do not count.
geo_anomaly.ban_duration_hint: Default 60, at most 10080 (7 days). Restored automatically; an admin can resume at any time. Changes apply to suspensions already running.
geo_anomaly.ban_effective: In effect: {{countries}} countries, or {{regions}} regions, or {{cities}} cities in one country, for {{polls}} checks; suspended {{minutes}} minutes
geo_anomaly.fresh_window_seconds_hint: How far behind its node's newest scan an address still counts as connected now. Default 120, range 20–900.
geo_anomaly.shared_exit_min_users_hint: This many accounts on one source at once make it a shared exit, set aside; subscription spread uses it too. Default 3, range 2–20.
geo_anomaly.ban_max_per_poll_hint: Default 20, at most 200; the rest wait for the next poll.
geo_anomaly.lift_max_per_poll_hint: Default 20, at most 200; the rest wait for the next poll.
geo_anomaly.infra_refresh_minutes_hint: Default 5, range 1–60; a change applies after the next refresh.

risk.min_days_hint: Days a province or device must appear on within the fetch window (bounded by sub-log retention), counted as calendar days in the panel timezone; at most the window's days.

help.label: About this tab
help.queue: One row per account that needs a look, most urgent first: flagged and auto-suspended, flagged, auto-suspended, suspect, then latest change. The bell counts only accounts that need action now (flagged or auto-suspended). Dismissing removes an account until a new or more severe signal appears; trusting exempts it from location checks for good. Observe-only signals never change an account; the panel only suspends on its own when automatic suspension is on.
help.live: The addresses connected on every panel at the last traffic poll or refresh. It is a snapshot and may be stale; its time is shown above. A refresh never counts as a detector sample.
help.records: Every entry into or out of suspect or flagged, every automatic suspension applied or lifted, and every admin dismiss or trust action, each with the reason at the time and never an IP, a name or a note.
help.policy: One card per detector: a switch, a preset, the key thresholds, the rest under Advanced. An empty field is the shipped default. Group exceptions are at the bottom and save separately.

docker.prepare: Use Linux Docker Engine with a standard Compose implementation. Create a private project with ./config and ./data directories. Save compose.yaml in the project root and node-credential.txt as ./config/node-credential.txt before validation or deployment. Compose mounts config read-only and data read-write. Preserve the complete project directory when reinstalling or updating.
docker.credential: Transfer node-credential.txt through a private channel, place it under ./config, and restrict read access. The generated validation refuses symlink, directory, or missing credential paths before Compose starts. Never put credentials in command arguments, environment variables, tracing, shell history, or shared logs.
docker.start: Start the generated Agent service. If the advanced remote-upgrade option was enabled, the generated isolated updater also starts with no network and alone receives the root-equivalent Docker socket. Dynamic listeners require host networking. Never mount the socket into the Agent or use privileged containers.
docker.check: Check the generated service or services, the application version and Agent status in Passwall Sub Panel, then configure nodes separately; a heartbeat does not prove the proxy core is running. When enabled, the updater accepts official exact releases only and restores the retained previous container unless the replacement synchronizes and converges. Back up the complete project directory, especially config and data.

manual.prepare: Use a connected administrator device to download the exact two public release files shown here, then transfer them with node-credential.txt and node-config.json through a trusted channel. The target needs only local archive and checksum tools; it does not need GitHub access. Do not overwrite an existing installation or data directory.
manual.download_verify: Verify the already transferred archive against exactly one matching SHA-256 entry. The command performs no network access. Checksums verify integrity against the same trusted release publisher, not an independent digital signature. Stop if it fails.
manual.extract: Read only the exact application binary, LICENSE, and NOTICE as regular files from the selected archive. Windows requires PowerShell 5.1 with .NET Framework 4.7.2 or newer, or PowerShell 7, to inspect ZIP entry attributes; stop rather than skip checks if that capability is unavailable. Never extract arbitrary paths, links, or file ownership into system directories. If a destination already exists, stop and inspect it manually.
manual.credential: node-config.json records non-sensitive installation values; it is not a daemon configuration loaded through --config. Never put credentials in command arguments, environment variables, tracing, shell history, or logs. The persistent data directory retains identity, SQLite counters, downloaded cores, and confirmed runtime state. Before manual updates, back up matching credentials, the installation record, and data together.
manual.run: Check the application version, then run in the foreground and keep this terminal open. Configure nodes separately in Passwall Sub Panel after the Agent connects. Use free ports at or above 1024 for unprivileged Linux / macOS operation. This method registers no system service and installs neither systemd nor the remote upgrade helper; use the recommended installer for a long-running Linux service. Stop the old machine before reusing its credential.

method_steps.linux:
1. Save the server and generate the private script for an exact release.
2. Transfer the script to the target Linux server and run the provided commands as root.
3. Confirm the service and heartbeat, then configure inbounds separately on the Nodes page.
method_steps.github:
1. Run the default public command on the target Linux/systemd host; it uses Stable unless this server's saved channel is Beta.
2. Enter the endpoint, Agent ID and credential shown here when prompted.
3. Use the install-only command when configuration must be deferred; finish later with sudo pn connect.
method_steps.docker:
1. Save the server and generate compose.yaml plus node-credential.txt.
2. Put compose.yaml in the project root and node-credential.txt in ./config; retain the generated ./data directory. The updater is enabled by default; turn it off from Advanced if this host must not expose its Docker socket.
3. Preserve the complete project directory, confirm the generated service(s) and heartbeat, then configure inbounds separately.
method_steps.manual:
1. Select the target OS, architecture and exact reviewed release, then generate all server-specific files.
2. Download the listed public release files on a connected device and transfer all four files to the target.
3. Follow the offline verification and foreground-run steps in Advanced; no target-side GitHub access is required.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.subtitle: Troubleshoot traffic polling, user status sync and panel connections.
diagnostics.help: This page summarises what PSP's background jobs record about themselves, to troubleshoot traffic polling, user status sync and panel connections. Every number is a running total over the statistics window, which opens when the panel starts and again whenever the statistics are cleared, so "17 times" does not mean it is still happening. The page refreshes every minute, and most problems show whether they have grown since you opened the page. A zero proves little while the window is short, so no verdict is given until the window spans three poll intervals; errors that have already happened are listed at once. "Typical" means half the cases were faster; "95% within X" means only 5% were slower; both are estimated from buckets. All raw metrics are kept at the bottom of the page and can be copied or downloaded for support.

push_capacity_zero.title: The traffic service did not start
push_capacity_zero.impact: Neither traffic polling nor quota safety refreshes will run: metering, over-quota suspension and live-IP collection have all stopped, so the numbers for those areas mean nothing.
push_capacity_zero.action: Check the server's startup log for errors, fix them and restart the panel.

poll_dead.title: Traffic polling has stopped: not one poll in {{window}}
poll_dead.impact: Traffic is no longer metered, over-quota users are not suspended automatically, and quota safety refreshes, live-IP collection and location checks have stopped too. Expiry does not depend on traffic polling and is unaffected.
poll_dead.action: Check the server's log for errors or a crash, fix the cause and restart the panel.

poll_errors.title: {{errors}} of {{polls}} polls were skipped entirely because the user list could not be read
poll_errors.impact: Those polls metered no traffic and checked no quotas. An unreachable panel is not counted here.
poll_errors.action: Check that the database is reachable and its disk is not full.

poll_behind.title: About {{missing}} polls are missing ({{polls}} ran; the interval implies at least {{expected}})
poll_behind.impact: Some polls were skipped: a poll plus the rollup after it may have taken longer than the interval, or polling was briefly held back. No traffic is lost, since the next poll picks it up, but over-quota suspensions are delayed.
poll_behind.action: Check the longest poll duration under Traffic polling and the slowest operations under Panel requests on this page; if needed, lengthen the traffic poll interval in Settings.

lifecycle_errors.title: {{errors}} of {{checks}} status checks failed ({{pct}})
lifecycle_errors.impact: These carry enable and disable, expiry and traffic caps. Where the status did not reach the panel, a disabled, expired or over-quota user may still be able to connect through it.
lifecycle_errors.origin: Quota safety refreshes had no failures in this window, so none of these came from them. They came from admin actions, automatic suspend and resume (including over-quota and location suspensions triggered by polling), sync-task retries, or the startup and periodic repairs.
lifecycle_errors.breakdown: By step: {{stages}}; by panel type: {{kinds}}. "Panel not found" and "Write" mean the write itself failed; "Read-back" and "Read-back mismatch" mean the write went out but could not be confirmed; "Saving the result" means the panel was updated and confirmed, and only PSP's own record failed.
lifecycle_errors.retry: Failures caused by admin actions, membership changes or automatic suspend and resume are recorded in Sync tasks, where you can see the error and retry. The periodic repair also re-checks every user and fixes whatever is still out of step. Every failed retry counts again, so this is not the number of affected users.
lifecycle_errors.action: Open Sync tasks and look for unfinished or cancelled user tasks and their errors; then check on Servers that the panels are reachable and native nodes are online.
lifecycle_errors.log_note: This finds two kinds of line: one per user, carrying only the first error; and one per failed client, whose message reads "shared-client lifecycle push failed for a client", carrying the panel id (panel_id) and the step that failed (stage), so failures on different panels can be told apart.

push_errors.title: {{errors}} of {{attempted}} quota safety refreshes failed ({{pct}})
push_errors.impact: The remaining allowance stored on the panel is out of date for those users. While PSP is running it still suspends over-quota users at the next poll; the panel relies on this allowance only while PSP is offline. The part that failed to write to a panel is also counted under status sync failures, so the two counts overlap.
push_errors.retry: These failures are not queued as sync tasks: the user is refreshed again the next time they use traffic, and the periodic repair also catches up.
push_errors.action: Check on Servers that the panels involved are reachable.

push_backlog.title: {{cycles}} polls skipped their quota refreshes because refreshes from an earlier poll were still queued ({{suppressed}} refreshes skipped)
push_backlog.impact: Panels are not keeping up with the polling pace. Skipped users are refreshed in a later poll once they use traffic again; enable, disable and expiry do not travel this path and are unaffected.
push_backlog.action: Under Panel requests on this page, see which kind of operation is slowest, and use Test connection on Servers; if it keeps happening, lengthen the traffic poll interval.

liveip_incomplete.title: Live IPs were incomplete {{incomplete}} times (user × poll)
liveip_incomplete.impact: A panel returned no live IPs during polling, so those users' live-IP counts and location verdicts are only "at least". The same user counts again every poll.
liveip_incomplete.sui: S-UI panels are connected: S-UI does not report live IPs, so users on those panels count every poll and this number keeps growing. If only S-UI users are affected, this is expected.
liveip_incomplete.action: Check on Servers that the other panels are reachable, and search the server log for the keywords below to see which panel did not answer.
liveip_incomplete.log: live client IPs unavailable for this panel

history_write_errors.title: Live connections could not be written to the connection history in {{errors}} polls
history_write_errors.impact: The Risk Center's connection history has gaps for those periods; they are not backfilled. Polling itself is unaffected.
history_write_errors.action: Check that the database accepts writes and its disk is not full.

flag_write_errors.title: Flag records failed to save {{errors}} times (each failure may cover several records)
flag_write_errors.impact: The flags, automatic suspensions or resumes themselves took effect; only their entries are missing from the Risk Center's Records.
flag_write_errors.action: Check that the database accepts writes and its disk is not full.

geo_auto_errors.title: Automatic location suspension failed {{suspend}} times; automatic lifting failed {{lift}} times
geo_auto_errors.impact: When a suspension fails, the user judged to be elsewhere keeps working until the trigger builds up again; a failed lift is retried at the next poll.
geo_auto_errors.action: Review the automatically suspended users in the Risk Center and act on them by hand if needed.
geo_auto_errors.log: geo auto-suspension: suspend failed · geo auto-suspension: lift failed

node_sync_refused.title: Native-node sync reports were refused {{count}} times (incompatible version {{proto}}, invalid report {{invalid}})
node_sync_refused.impact: A refused sync brings back no user changes, and the traffic and online state it carried are not recorded. An incompatible version gets every sync refused, so that node is effectively offline.
node_sync_refused.action: Check the node's compatibility on Servers and upgrade the node agent or the panel so their versions match.

sso_claim_silent.title: Single sign-on brought back nothing the role or group rules read (counted per kind: role {{role}}, group {{group}})
sso_claim_silent.impact: Those users kept their existing role and group; if the identity provider has revoked their access, the panel still keeps it.
sso_claim_silent.action: Check the single sign-on attribute mapping in Settings, and confirm the identity provider actually sends those attributes.

capability_gaps.title: Some users have limits their panel cannot apply (IP limit {{ip}} times, device limit {{device}} times)
capability_gaps.impact: These limits are written to the panel but have no effect: S-UI and PSP native nodes support neither the IP limit nor the device limit, and 3X-UI below 3.7.0 cannot store the device limit. Every check counts again while this lasts; it is a standing condition, not a fault.
capability_gaps.note: Also, the device limit is not enforced on any panel today; 3X-UI 3.7.0 and later only store the value. A zero here does not mean device limits are in effect.
capability_gaps.action: On Servers, check each panel's type and version against the explanation above to see which cannot apply these limits; the limit fields in the user editor also name those panels. Move these users to a panel that can, or upgrade the panel.
capability_gaps.log: panel cannot enforce a setting PSP is pushing

self_check.title: Consistency checks
self_check.note: Checks that related numbers agree. Only for troubleshooting the statistics themselves; they do not affect the verdict above.

poll_ms.pass: {{observed}} poll-duration records match the {{expected}} polls started (a difference of 1 is allowed).
poll_ms.fail: {{observed}} poll-duration records against {{expected}} polls started, a difference of more than 1: more than one poll was running when this was read, usually a "Poll now" overlapping a scheduled poll, or a manual poll started while another was stuck.

push_enqueue.pass: {{started}} quota safety refreshes ran, no more than the {{enqueued}} queued.
push_enqueue.fail: {{started}} quota safety refreshes ran, more than the {{enqueued}} queued. Refreshes still queued when the statistics were cleared were counted as queued before the clear and as run after it, so the excess, the number that were queued then, stays for the whole window; it is harmless. Report it to the developers only if it appears in a window that has not been cleared since the panel started.

common.failing: Something needs action; see the top of the page.
common.attention: Something needs attention; see the top of the page.
common.notices: There are notices; see the top of the page.
common.measuring: The window is still short; a verdict in about {{remaining}}.
common.measuring_unknown: The traffic poll interval is unknown, so no verdict yet.
common.blackout: The window is shorter than one poll interval; numbers are held back.
common.inhibited: Traffic polling is not running, so this part can't be judged.

poll.title: Traffic polling
poll.purpose: Reads usage from every panel at the poll interval, meters traffic from it and suspends over-quota users, then runs the quota safety refresh and collects live IPs for the Risk Center. When it stops, the quota safety refresh and the live-IP and risk data stop with it; the other areas keep counting.
poll.ok: On schedule: one poll every {{interval}}, {{polls}} in this window.

stages.title: Where a poll's time goes (average)
stages.note: "Read panels" covers each panel's traffic and live IPs. Suspensions triggered during a poll are written to the panel on the spot, so "Aggregate, meter and judge" and "Location suspensions" can also include time spent waiting on panels.

lifecycle.title: User status sync
lifecycle.purpose: Writes each user's enabled state, expiry, traffic cap and connection limits to every panel they are on. Disabling, pausing and over-quota cut-off all take effect through this step. Each time, the panel's current state is read first: if it matches, nothing is written.
lifecycle.ok: {{checks}} checks in this window; {{skipped}} needed no change.
lifecycle.idle: No user was checked in this window: users' clients may not be set up on the panels yet, or there were no admin actions and no users to refresh in this period.
lifecycle.not_provisioned: Another {{count}} checks were skipped because the client is not yet set up on the panel.

limits.title: Can the limits be applied?
limits.ip_gaps: IP limit: {{count}} checks involved a panel without IP-limit support
limits.ip_none: IP limit: no limit set on an unsupported panel in this window
limits.device: Device limit: PSP does not enforce it on any panel today; the value is only stored on the panel
limits.device_gaps: Another {{count}} checks involved a panel that cannot even store the device limit
limits.servers_note: Whether each node can actually enforce the IP limit is shown on the Servers page.

floor.title: Quota safety refresh
floor.purpose: After each poll, writes the remaining allowance of users who used traffic, have a traffic cap and are still under it to the panels. That way a panel can cut a user off by itself when the allowance runs out, even while PSP is offline. While PSP is running, over-quota suspension is done by traffic polling and does not depend on this step.
floor.ok: {{count}} refreshes in this window, about {{perPoll}} per poll.
floor.idle: No user needed a refresh in this window: nobody with a traffic cap, still under it, used traffic.

panel_api.title: Panel requests (3X-UI)
panel_api.purpose: Count, failures and duration of every request PSP sends to 3X-UI panels, by kind of operation, without telling panels apart.
panel_api.ok: {{count}} requests to 3X-UI panels in this window, {{pct}} failed.
panel_api.idle: No requests were sent to 3X-UI panels in this window.
panel_api.note_scope: 3X-UI panels only; S-UI and PSP native nodes are not counted. Each automatic retry counts separately.
panel_api.note_get_client: "Read client" failures include normal lookups for clients not yet created, which are not necessarily faults.
panel_api.note_timeout: A longest time close to 30 s means the request hit its timeout.

liveip.title: Live IPs and risk data
liveip.purpose: How well the Risk Center's data is being collected: whether live IPs are read in full, whether records are saved, and whether automatic suspensions go through. For the verdicts themselves, see the Risk Center.
liveip.ok: Every poll read live IPs from every panel; about {{judged}} users judged per poll on average.
liveip.idle: No user was judged for live IPs in this window. Users are judged even when nobody is online, so this usually means no user has a client set up on any panel yet, or polling could not list users' clients: search the server log for "traffic poll shared-client list failed"; where it appears, shared clients' traffic went unmetered in those polls too.

kpi.incomplete_caption: the same user counts every poll
kpi.risk_none: did not run in this window

liveip.sui_note: S-UI panels are connected: S-UI does not report live IPs, so users on those panels count as incomplete every poll.

node.title: Native nodes
node.purpose: Whether host metric reports and sync requests from PSP native nodes are received and saved.
node.ok: {{count}} host metric reports received in this window.
node.idle: No reports from native nodes in this window.
node.not_applicable: No PSP native nodes are connected.

system.goroutines_note: Developer information: only worth a look if it keeps rising across refreshes while the load stays flat.

raw.title: All raw metrics
raw.search: Search by name, label or description
raw.previous_note: Viewing the data from before clearing (up to {{time}}), read-only.
raw.blackout_note: The window is shorter than one poll interval; numbers are for reference only, and a zero does not mean healthy.
raw.absence_note: Metrics without labels always appear, so a missing one means an older server. Labelled metrics appear only once something has happened, so a missing one means zero.
raw.absent: This server version does not have this metric

raw.quantile_note: Percentiles are estimated from buckets; under 10 samples, read the maximum instead.

reset.title: Clear the statistics and start again?
reset.message: All {{window}} of statistics will be cleared, including the risk and native-node counts shown on this page; the Risk Center's own data is not affected. Afterwards this page keeps the data from before clearing for download until you leave it.
reset.kept: Cleared. The {{window}} of statistics from before can be downloaded until you leave this page.

psp_poll_total.label: Traffic polls
psp_poll_total.desc: Traffic polls started, scheduled and manual ("Poll now") alike. Normally about the window divided by the poll interval.

psp_poll_error_total.label: Polls that failed outright
psp_poll_error_total.desc: Polls abandoned because the user list could not be read, usually a database problem. An unreachable panel or a single user's error is not counted here.

psp_poll_ms.label: Poll duration
psp_poll_ms.desc: Time from the start to the end of one poll, excluding the quota safety refreshes that run afterwards in the background. Should stay well below the poll interval.

psp_poll_stage_ms.label: Poll duration by stage
psp_poll_stage_ms.desc: How long each stage of a poll took. "Read panels" is usually the largest share; it is time spent waiting on the network.

psp_poll_interval_ms.label: Current poll interval
psp_poll_interval_ms.desc: The interval traffic polling actually runs on. After the setting changes, the new interval applies once the next poll has run; the peak is the longest interval used in this window.

psp_poll_users.label: Users read per poll
psp_poll_users.desc: All users read per poll, including admins and disabled users.

psp_poll_active_users.label: Users with traffic per poll
psp_poll_active_users.desc: Users whose traffic changed in a poll, whether or not they have a traffic cap.

psp_poll_panels.label: Panels read per poll
psp_poll_panels.desc: Panels read per poll; only panels that host at least one user's client are counted.

psp_lifecycle_sync_total.label: Status checks
psp_lifecycle_sync_total.desc: Checks comparing a user's intended status with what a panel actually holds, counted once per client per panel. Triggered by the post-poll quota safety refresh, admin actions, automatic suspend and resume, sync tasks and the periodic repair.

psp_lifecycle_sync_skipped_total.label: Already in sync
psp_lifecycle_sync_skipped_total.desc: Checks where the panel already matched, so nothing was written. The higher the share, the fewer writes the panels receive.

psp_lifecycle_sync_write_total.label: Writes to panels
psp_lifecycle_sync_write_total.desc: Writes issued because something differed, or because the panel's current state could not be read. These are attempts; failures are also counted under "Sync failures".

psp_lifecycle_sync_write_reason_total.label: Why writes happened
psp_lifecycle_sync_write_reason_total.desc: The reason for each write, taken from the first field that differed. "Panel state unreadable" means the read failed or the client was missing, so PSP wrote without comparing.

psp_lifecycle_sync_not_provisioned_total.label: Skipped: not set up yet
psp_lifecycle_sync_not_provisioned_total.desc: Checks skipped because the user's client is not yet confirmed on the panel. Normal briefly after adding nodes or users; steady growth means setting up clients keeps failing.

psp_lifecycle_sync_error_total.label: Sync failures
psp_lifecycle_sync_error_total.desc: User status syncs that failed: panel not found, write failed, read-back failed or did not match, or PSP could not save the result (the panel was already updated then). Counted per client; every failed retry counts again.

psp_lifecycle_sync_error_stage_total.label: Sync failures by step
psp_lifecycle_sync_error_stage_total.desc: Sync failures by the step that failed: panel not found, the write, reading back after the write, a read-back that does not match, saving the result. The steps add up to "Sync failures". Each failed client is also logged once with its panel id.

psp_lifecycle_sync_error_panel_kind_tota.label: Sync failures by panel type
psp_lifecycle_sync_error_panel_kind_tota.desc: Sync failures by the type of panel the client is on: 3X-UI, S-UI, PSP native node; "Unknown" when the panel could not be found. The types add up to "Sync failures".

psp_lifecycle_quota_delta_bytes.label: Panel cap drift
psp_lifecycle_quota_delta_bytes.desc: How far the traffic cap stored on the panel was from the intended value at each check. Used to size the tolerance; not something to watch day to day.

psp_lifecycle_quota_band_skip_total.label: Within tolerance
psp_lifecycle_quota_band_skip_total.desc: Checks where the panel's traffic cap differed but stayed within tolerance, so it did not by itself cause a write (another field may still have).

psp_capability_gap_total.label: Limits the panel cannot apply
psp_capability_gap_total.desc: Checks where a user has an IP or device limit their panel does not support. Counted again at every check while the situation lasts.

psp_ip_limit_enforcement_total.label: IP-limit enforcement probes
psp_ip_limit_enforcement_total.desc: Results of probing each 3X-UI node's fail2ban, which decides whether an IP limit can actually be enforced. Per-node results are on the Servers page.

psp_user_client_count.label: Clients per user
psp_user_client_count.desc: How many clients a user has across all panels, recorded each time the user is synced. Usually about the number of panels the user's group spans.

psp_user_clients_per_panel.label: Clients per user per panel
psp_user_clients_per_panel.desc: How many clients one user needs on a single panel. Above 1, each client carries its own copy of the IP limit, so the effective allowance is multiplied.

psp_sync_user_lifecycle_ms.label: Per-user sync time
psp_sync_user_lifecycle_ms.desc: Time to sync one user's status to all of their panels. Panels are handled in parallel, so this is roughly the slowest panel.

psp_push_client_config_total.label: Quota safety refreshes
psp_push_client_config_total.desc: Refreshes of the remaining allowance on the panels for users who used traffic, have a traffic cap and are still under it; at most once per user per poll.

psp_push_client_config_error_total.label: Quota safety refresh failures
psp_push_client_config_error_total.desc: Quota safety refreshes that failed. They are not queued as sync tasks; the user is refreshed again the next time they use traffic or at the next periodic repair.

psp_push_client_config_ms.label: Quota safety refresh duration
psp_push_client_config_ms.desc: Time one quota safety refresh took once it started, excluding time spent queued.

psp_push_sem_capacity.label: Concurrent refresh limit
psp_push_sem_capacity.desc: The most quota safety refreshes that run at once. Fixed at 8; 0 means the traffic service did not start.

psp_push_sem_inflight.label: Refreshes running
psp_push_sem_inflight.desc: Quota safety refreshes running right now; the peak is the highest in this window.

psp_push_sem_waiting.label: Refreshes waiting
psp_push_sem_waiting.desc: Quota safety refreshes waiting for a slot right now; a peak that keeps growing means the panels cannot keep up.

psp_push_sem_wait_ms.label: Queue wait
psp_push_sem_wait_ms.desc: Time each quota safety refresh waited before starting, including those that did not wait (about 0). Refreshes still queued when read are not yet included, so this understates a backlog.

psp_push_sem_carryover_total.label: Polls skipped for backlog
psp_push_sem_carryover_total.desc: Polls that skipped all their quota safety refreshes because refreshes from an earlier poll were still queued. Cannot happen on the first poll after start; normally 0.

psp_push_suppressed_total.label: Refreshes skipped for backlog
psp_push_suppressed_total.desc: Individual quota safety refreshes skipped because of that backlog. A skipped user is refreshed in a later poll once they use traffic again.

psp_poll_floor_push_enqueued_total.label: Quota safety refreshes queued
psp_poll_floor_push_enqueued_total.desc: Quota safety refreshes handed to the queue. Normally almost equal to "Quota safety refreshes"; the difference is still queued.

psp_panel_rtt_ms.label: Panel request time
psp_panel_rtt_ms.desc: Time of one request from PSP to a 3X-UI panel, by operation, including automatic re-login. Close to 30 s means the request hit its timeout.

psp_panel_op_total.label: Panel requests
psp_panel_op_total.desc: Requests PSP sent to 3X-UI panels, by operation; each automatic retry counts separately. S-UI and native nodes are not counted.

psp_panel_op_error_total.label: Panel request failures
psp_panel_op_error_total.desc: 3X-UI requests that returned an error: connection failure, HTTP error or refusal by the panel. "Read client" also counts a lookup for a client not yet created, which is not necessarily a fault.

psp_user_live_ips.label: Live IPs per user
psp_user_live_ips.desc: Distinct source IPs per judged user per poll, from the panels' memory of roughly the last 30 minutes. Only "at least" when the read was incomplete.

psp_live_ip_users_incomplete_total.label: Incomplete live-IP reads
psp_live_ip_users_incomplete_total.desc: User-poll occurrences where a panel holding the user's clients returned no live IPs; the same user counts again every poll. S-UI panels do not report live IPs, so this keeps growing while users are on S-UI.

psp_user_concurrent_ips.label: Concurrent sources per user
psp_user_concurrent_ips.desc: Concurrent sources per judged user per poll (IPv6 folded by /64, ignored addresses excluded): the number the location check judges.

psp_live_ip_stale_total.label: Stale live addresses
psp_live_ip_stale_total.desc: Addresses treated as stale at judging time (not seen within the freshness window of their node's latest scan). Zero for hours on a busy 3X-UI fleet may mean timestamps stopped arriving.

psp_live_ip_excluded_total.label: Excluded sources
psp_live_ip_excluded_total.desc: Sources set aside before judging, by rule: shared, on the ignore list, PSP's own nodes or relays, internal addresses.

psp_geo_verdict_total.label: Location verdicts
psp_geo_verdict_total.desc: Distribution of per-user location verdicts per poll. See the Risk Center for the users themselves.

psp_geo_over_tier_total.label: Tolerance exceeded, by level
psp_geo_over_tier_total.desc: Judged samples beyond tolerance, by the coarsest level exceeded (country, region, city).

psp_geo_spread_km.label: Source spread
psp_geo_spread_km.desc: Distance between the two farthest concurrent sources of one user, after subtracting location accuracy; only users with two or more located sources.

psp_geo_samples_spaced_total.label: Skipped: judged too recently
psp_geo_samples_spaced_total.desc: Users not judged again because their last verdict was less than half a poll interval ago, usually after a manual "Poll now".

psp_geo_auto_suspension_total.label: Automatic location suspensions
psp_geo_auto_suspension_total.desc: Outcomes of automatic location suspension and lifting. "Suspend failed" and "Lift failed" are failures; "Lifted by admin" against "Suspended" estimates the false-positive rate.

psp_infra_addresses.label: Infrastructure addresses
psp_infra_addresses.desc: Addresses currently excluded from location checks as PSP's own nodes or relays. Zero while nodes are configured means the refresh is failing.

psp_infra_address_resolve_failures_total.label: Node hostname lookups failed
psp_infra_address_resolve_failures_total.desc: Node or relay hostnames that failed to resolve during the infrastructure refresh; the previous addresses are kept. If it persists, check node hostnames and DNS.

psp_live_connections.label: Live connections
psp_live_connections.desc: Connections in the latest stored live snapshot: what the Risk Center's Live tab shows.

psp_live_conn_refresh_total.label: Live snapshot refreshes
psp_live_conn_refresh_total.desc: Outcomes of the Risk Center's "Refresh now". "Failed" or "Partial" means some panels could not be read on demand.

psp_connection_history_write_errors_tota.label: Connection history write failures
psp_connection_history_write_errors_tota.desc: Polls whose judged connections could not be written to the connection history. Those periods stay missing; they are not backfilled.

psp_flag_record_write_errors_total.label: Flag record write failures
psp_flag_record_write_errors_total.desc: Flag-record writes that failed; each may carry several records. The flags, automatic suspensions or resumes themselves took effect; only their records are missing.

psp_risk_refresh_total.label: Risk signal runs
psp_risk_refresh_total.desc: Outcomes of risk-signal recomputation (hourly by default). Repeated "Partial", "Waiting for node addresses" or "Failed" means the Risk Center is judging from old data.

psp_node_host_report_total.label: Host metric reports
psp_node_host_report_total.desc: Outcomes of handling native-node host metric reports. A failed report never fails the node's sync itself.

psp_node_host_history_total.label: Host metric history
psp_node_host_history_total.desc: Results of writing host metric history: inserted, throttled, duplicate, storage error.

psp_node_host_persist_ms.label: Host metric save time
psp_node_host_persist_ms.desc: Time to save one host metric report; the budget is 500 ms.

psp_node_host_snapshot_bytes.label: Host metric size
psp_node_host_snapshot_bytes.desc: Encoded size of one stored host metric snapshot; the limit is 128 KiB.

psp_node_host_rollup_total.label: Hourly host metric rollups
psp_node_host_rollup_total.desc: Results of the hourly per-node host metric rollup; "error" should be 0.

psp_node_host_pruned_rows_total.label: Host metrics pruned
psp_node_host_pruned_rows_total.desc: Host metric rows removed by retention; steady growth is normal.

psp_node_sync_refused_total.label: Node sync reports refused
psp_node_sync_refused_total.desc: Authenticated native-node sync reports this panel refused. "Incompatible version" means the node is effectively offline.

psp_node_policy_status_dropped_total.label: Access control status reports dropped
psp_node_policy_status_dropped_total.desc: Access control status reports dropped because their format, contents or node capabilities are invalid; config and roster synchronization continues.

psp_dest_pruned_rows_total.label: Access control rows cleaned up
psp_dest_pruned_rows_total.desc: Rows removed by connected access control cleanup tasks. Expired exemptions are cleaned up hourly; other retention tasks arrive in later stages.

psp_dest_policy_publish_total.label: Access control versions published
psp_dest_policy_publish_total.desc: Successfully committed access control versions, by trigger. Unchanged requests, failures and concurrent attempts that lost the commit do not count.

psp_dest_policy_publish_rejected_total.label: Access control publication checks failed
psp_dest_policy_publish_rejected_total.desc: Publication attempts rejected by validation with their error saved. Storage failures and superseded attempts do not count; the previous published version stays in use.

psp_dest_policy_compile_total.label: Access control candidate compilation calls
psp_dest_policy_compile_total.desc: Each compiler call has one result: candidate produced, complete cache reused, fallback or failure. Cached results must complete their storage transaction; this does not establish node acknowledgement.

psp_dest_policy_compile_ms.label: Access control compilation time
psp_dest_policy_compile_ms.desc: Total time per compiler call, including cache reads, storage and failed attempts, in milliseconds.

psp_dest_list_refresh_total.label: Access control list refresh attempts
psp_dest_list_refresh_total.desc: One result per executed refresh. Broad entries mean a remote list was rejected with previous content retained, or a category was successfully saved after filtering. Download, cancellation and storage errors count as failed.

psp_saml_acs_failure_total.label: SAML sign-ins refused
psp_saml_acs_failure_total.desc: Refused SAML sign-ins (and sign-in starts), by reason. Configuration reasons point at identity-provider settings; "Assertion replayed" needs investigating.

psp_sso_claim_silent_total.label: Single sign-ins without role or group
psp_sso_claim_silent_total.desc: Single sign-ins where role or group rules exist but the identity provider sent none of the attributes they read, counted per kind: one sign-in can count once for each. The existing role and group were kept.
